scorecards.inningsCommentary: Entering the third innings with the match balance in flux, Bangladesh sought to extend their lead and set a decisive fourth-innings target. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 64 from Mushfiqur Rahim, complemented by a commanding 63-run stand between Liton Das and Mushfiqur Rahim that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.06 RPO. India's bowling response was spearheaded by Mohammed Shami (4/30), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Bangladesh's total of 213/10 (69.2 ov) closed their second innings, cementing a formidable target and transferring immense pressure onto the opposition.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Holkar Cricket Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Bangladesh posted 150/10 (58.3 ov) in their opening innings. In response, India countered with 493/6 (113.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: MA Agarwal 243 (332b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, MA Agarwal delivered a masterclass for India (243 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (India 64%) and allowing India to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Bangladesh faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. India's bowling unit, bolstered by UT Yadav (25 Runs & 5 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing India won by innings & 130 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: India's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Bangladesh produced fighting phases, India won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
